summary_units.title: Skeleton, cartilage, and ligaments
summary_units.summary: Skeleton & Bone Tissue ⚫ The skeleton is composed of bones, joints, cartilage and ligaments ⚫ Joints are the intersections between bones ⚫ Ligaments connects bone at the joints, thus reinforcing the joints Bone Tissue Function ⚫ Support ⚫ Provides significant structural support ⚫ Maintain a posture while accommodating large external forces ⚫ Attachment Sites ⚫ Site of attachment for tendons, muscles and ligaments, thus allows for the generation of movement through the muscular system ⚫ Leverage ⚫ Provides the levers and axes of rotation about which the muscular system generates the movement Cartilage ⚫ 2 main types of cartilages: ⚫ Articular(hyaline) cartilage ⚫ Covers the articulating ends of the bones in the free moving joints ⚫ Function: ⚫ Transit compressive forces across the joint ⚫ Allows motion in the joint with minimal friction ⚫ Redistributes contact stresses over a larger area ⚫ Protects underlying bones ⚫ Fibrocartilage ⚫ Acts as an intermediary between hyaline cartilage and other connective tissues ⚫ Can withstand high pressures ⚫ Refers to as articular disc, or meniscus Ligaments ⚫ Short bands of tough fibrous connective tissue that binds bones to bones ⚫ Provides support in one direction, and often blends with the capsule of the joint ⚫ Capsular ligaments: thickenings in the wall of the capsule ⚫ Extracapsular ligaments: outside the joint ⚫ Intra-articular ligaments: located inside the joint ⚫ Function: ⚫ Guide normal joint movement ⚫ Restrict abnormal joint movement Ligaments: Bone → bone • guides and limits movement
